title: Chapter 4: Under the old mill
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: Ines, Pim and Mother Sabela set out for the old mill at first light, with a lantern, a coil of rope and the torn map. Sabela walked slowly, and she explained on the way that the first glassblowers had not made the trees. They had found them already growing and had only learned to graft them. The stair behind the mill was choked with brambles, and Pim cut a path with his sweeping knife. At the bottom they came to an iron gate set into the rock. The water behind it was white with salt. Wagon ruts led to a side tunnel, where they found dozens of broken salt barrels stamped with the mark of Asche's trading house. Asche had been poisoning the spring so that the orchard would fail and the villagers would sell their plots cheaply. Pim wanted to run back and tell everyone at once. Sabela said that barrels could be denied unless someone saw who brought them, and that the spring would stay foul until the upper sluice was opened to flush it. While they argued, they heard boots on the stair. Two of Asche's carters came down with fresh barrels, led by Tomas, who had been hired to show them the way. Tomas stopped when he saw his cousin in the lantern light. One of the carters raised a pry bar, and Sabela stepped in front of Ines. The blow broke Sabela's arm. Tomas seized the carter and shouted that nobody had told him anyone would be hurt. In the struggle the lantern went into the water, and Ines took Pim's hand and led him through the iron gate into the dark.
